title: Series-Parallel 1: A Series Resistor Feeding a Parallel Pair
description: R1 (100 Ω) in series with R2 and R3 (200 Ω each) in parallel, across 12 V. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, find the total current, then work back out to every element.

tasks.question: What is the total resistance seen by the source?
What is the voltage across R1?
What is the voltage across R2 (and therefore across R3)?
What power is dissipated in R1?

hints: Reduce first: two equal 200 Ω resistors in parallel are 100 Ω. Redraw the circuit as R1 in series with that 100 Ω equivalent.
R_total = R1 + equivalent. I_total = 12 V ÷ R_total.
R1 carries the whole current, so V_R1 = I_total × 100. By KVL the parallel group gets 12 V minus V_R1.
Each parallel branch current is the group voltage divided by 200 Ω; the two branch currents must add back to I_total.
learningGoals: Identify series and parallel sections of a combination circuit.
Use reduce-and-redraw to find total resistance and current.
Expand the solution to individual element voltages and currents and verify with KVL and KCL.
disclaimer: Simulated bench exercise; not field experience.
